channel.description: What officeholders said each day from or about Mississippi, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, Mississippi, 2026-11-19: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Bennie Thompson)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Bennie Thompson, U.S. Representative from Mississippi: “While Americans were stranded in airports across the country, with many sleeping on the floor at their gates, the secretary boarded a luxury jet, flew to a college football game.” Unsettled. The AP reports Mullin flew on a government plane to the LSU-Texas game on Saturday, Nov. 14, the day after the Nov. 13 nationwide ground stop, which the AP says ended around 8:15 p.m. ET Friday. AskAmerica's FAA advisory data show airport-level ground stops continuing at some airports on Nov. 14 and 15, but neither source shows whether passengers were still stranded when the flight left.

item.title: Said & Checked, Mississippi, 2026-11-15: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Chris Van Hollen)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Chris Van Hollen, U.S. Senator from Maryland: “he wasn't recruited or picked by anybody in Washington. And in fact, Washington was very late in the game to supporting that.” Unsettled. The Associated Press reported on Oct. 20 that the Senate Democrats' main super PAC entered the Mississippi race "for the first time this year" with a $1.2 million ad two weeks before the election, which fits "late in the game". No page read addresses whether national Democrats recruited the candidate, and earlier national spending was not tested.
